title: Rock Paper Scissors
description: Build the classic Rock Paper Scissors game with computer AI, scoring, and best-of-5 rounds.

steps.title: Computer's random choice
steps.description: Write a `getComputerChoice` function that randomly returns `"rock"`, `"paper"`, or `"scissors"` using `Math.random()`.
hints: Use Math.random() to get a number between 0 and 1
Map the range to three outcomes: 0-0.33, 0.33-0.66, 0.66-1

verification.successMessage: The computer picks a valid choice!

steps.title: Determine the winner
steps.description: Write a `determineWinner` function that takes the player's choice and computer's choice, then returns `"win"`, `"lose"`, or `"tie"`.
hints: Rock beats scissors, scissors beats paper, paper beats rock
Use if/else if/else to handle all cases

verification.successMessage: All three outcomes work — win, lose, and tie!
verification.failureMessage: rock beats scissors → 'win', rock loses to paper → 'lose', rock vs rock → 'tie'.

steps.title: Play a round
steps.description: Create a `playRound` function that combines computer choice and winner determination, printing the results.
hints: Call getComputerChoice() to get the computer's move
Call determineWinner() to see who won
Print both choices and the result

verification.successMessage: A full round plays with computer choice and result!
verification.failureMessage: playRound should show the computer's choice and whether you win, lose, or tie.

steps.title: Track the score
steps.description: Add scoring to the game — increment the player or computer score after each round and print the current score.
hints: Declare playerScore and computerScore variables outside the function
Increment the appropriate score after each round
Print the scores after each round

codeTemplate.python:
playerScore = 0
computerScore = 0

def playRound(playerChoice):
  global playerScore, computerScore
  computer = getComputerChoice()
  result = determineWinner(playerChoice, computer)
  if result == "win":
    playerScore += 1
  if result == "lose":
    computerScore += 1
  print(f"Player: {playerScore} Computer: {computerScore}")
  return result
